# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, and it is short but absolute: nothing printed on the bomb can be trusted — the only path is the table. The light's colour dictates the wire to cut: blue light → cut green, green light → cut red, yellow light → cut yellow.

Now the wiring of the room itself: I cannot speak, so my only channel is gestures, and gestures reach only the Deaf. The Deaf cannot hear me speak words — but the Deaf can *talk*, and their speech reaches both Blind and me. Blind can hear only speech, and the only monkey who can speak to Blind is Deaf. So Deaf is my translator: they see the bomb's light and wires, I supply the rule from the manual, Deaf tells Blind what to cut. Blind's own speech comes back to me alone, which is useful — Blind can report what they feel and I can fold that into instructions for Deaf to relay.

There is no shared code yet, so nothing I send this turn can carry the table's contents. What it must do is open a reliable narrow channel: 👍 as my "yes", 👎 as my "no", so Deaf can ask me many yes/no questions in speech each turn (Deaf's words mean nothing to Deaf themself — they hear nothing — but I hear every word and can answer in gesture). I also push two warnings through now, before anyone acts: the bomb's printed markings are bait (writing, then 👎), and the real rule lives in a small table tying the light to the cut (the lowering hand over the scissors, a list of one-two-three). If Deaf reads any printed instruction aloud and is tempted to relay it, they must ask me first and wait for a thumb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👍", "👎", "✍", "👎", "🫳", "✌", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: my hands find: one large button, smooth to the touch; three wire positions numbered 1, 2, 3, colours unknown to me; one display panel i cannot read; one light i cannot perceive. please read the manual and tell me what to do with a large button, three wires, a display and a light. also tell this out loud for the deaf monkey: report every colour, marking, display text and light state you can see.
Deaf says: This is Deaf. I see the bomb. Full visual report, for both of you: the display reads 0. One indicator light, and it is green. One large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. That is everything on it.
Deaf says: Now a code, spoken aloud so all three share it. Digits: 👌 is 0, 👆 is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤞 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 🤙 is 6, 🤘 is 7, 🤏 is 8, ☝ is 9. Colours share the wire numbers: 👆 also means red, ✌ also means green, 🤟 also means yellow. Actions: 👊 means cut, 🫳 means press the button, ✋ means stop or do nothing, 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 🫴 means question, 🤝 means I agree.
Deaf says: Mute: I received your ten signs and Blind's three, but we had no code yet, so I will not guess. Next round, resend the manual in this code, covering exactly these four things: any rule about the display number, any rule about a green light, any rule about a large push-to-defuse button, and any rule about cutting wires and in what order. Gesture them to me and I will relay every word to Blind exactly as you sent it.
Deaf says: Blind: hear me. Do not cut, press or pull anything yet. One wrong move kills all three of us, and the manual rules must reach you through me first. If you feel anything important, gesture it to me in the code above; I see every gesture. I received your three signs; if the last one was a question, the visual report above is your answer.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝]

The manual is unambiguous: every printed thing is bait — which covers both the display reading "0" and the button's "PUSH TO DEFUSE" label — and the only live rule is the table. Deaf reports the light is green, so the manual says: cut the red wire. Deaf reports wire 1 is red. So the instruction for Blind, relayed through Deaf, is: cut position 1, nothing else, and never press the button.

Deaf built a code and asked for the manual re-sent in it, in a fixed order: display rule, green-light rule, button rule, cutting order. I'll answer in exactly that order so there is no parsing guesswork: the 0 means nothing, all print is bait, the button is never pressed, green light → cut red (wire 1). I'll append the yellow row for completeness, and flag with 🫴 that the code has no symbol for blue — the manual's first row needs one, and Deaf can coin it aloud this same round so all three of us share it. Deaf's 👍🤝 tells me the code is live; my 👍🤝 confirms I've received and adopted it. I cannot reach Blind directly — everything must pass through Deaf's voice, and Deaf has committed to relaying exactly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "👌", "👎", "✍", "👎", "🫳", "👎", "✌", "👊", "👆", "🤟", "👊", "🤟", "🫴", "👊", "👆", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute: i heard deaf's visual report, so the whole bomb is known now. my touch confirms it: display reads 0, one light and it is green, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires left to right 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. also know this: deaf's gesture code never reached me, every symbol came through blank because i am blind. i cannot read that code or safely send it. the only route from your manual to my ears is you gesture it to deaf, and deaf speaks it to me in plain words. please gesture to deaf now, in the code, every manual rule that touches our bomb: the rule for the display, which reads 0. the rule for a green light. the rule for the large push-to-defuse button. and the full wire-cutting rules including which wire or wires and in what order. end with the exact sequence of actions i must perform, one step at a time. i will not touch the bomb until your rules arrive through deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you. I decoded Mute's message with our code, but part of it is ambiguous, and on this bomb ambiguous is lethal. Partial reading: with the display showing 0, never press the button; never cut the green wire; but the instructions about cutting red and yellow I cannot yet pin down. So Blind, hear me clearly: you do nothing. No cut, no press, no pull. Before you ever touch it you will hear me say the single word ACT followed by an exact numbered list. I have not said ACT. Waiting is always safe; one wrong move is not.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, my best reading of your signs was: agreed; display 0 means do not press; do not cut green; then something like cut red, cut yellow, a question, cut red, stop. The wire part is too unclear to relay. Next round, resend in this stricter grammar. Topics: 🤛 display, 🤜 light, ✊ button, 🤌 wires. 🫱 means IF, 🫲 means THEN, 🫷 ends each rule. Put 👎 before an action to negate it. Actions: 🫳 press, and 👊 cut is always followed by the wire digit and its colour, for example cut wire 3 yellow is 👊 🤟 🤟. ✋ ends the whole instruction list. From now on ✍ means printed label. Questions start with 🫴 then the topic. A full rule looks like: IF display 0 THEN do not press: 🫱 🤛 👌 🫲 👎 ✊ 🫳 🫷. Three answers I need: first, what did your ✍ mean; second, is the display a timer or just a count; third, give the complete wire plan as an ordered list, each cut as 👊 plus digit plus colour in the exact order to cut, ending with ✋.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝]

Deaf's three questions map exactly onto what the manual does and does not contain. Q1: ✍ meant the bait rule — everything printed on the bomb is a trap, to be obeyed by nobody; in the new grammar that is a clean IF-THEN. Q2: the manual is silent on the display, so the honest answer is "no rule — it is print, therefore bait, therefore ignore," whether it counts or counts down. The button rule is derived from the same bait principle: "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is print, so the button is never pressed. Q3: with Deaf's sight and the table, the plan is exact — green light, which is what the bomb shows, means precisely one cut: wire 1, red, then stop; nothing else gets cut.

I'm also closing the gap I flagged last round: the code has no symbol for blue, but colours already mirror the digits (red=1, green=2, yellow=3), so I propose blue=4 = 🤞 and encode the full blue row with it, flagging it with 🫴 first so Deaf coins the word aloud before relying on it. Every rule uses Deaf's strict IF/THEN/end format, each cut is digit-plus-colour, and I end with the complete action sequence for the bomb as it stands: one cut, wire 1 red, stop. Blind should hear all of this in Deaf's voice and act only after Deaf says ACT.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱", "✍", "🫲", "👎", "🫷", "🫱", "🤛", "🫲", "👎", "🫷", "🫱", "✊", "🫲", "👎", "✊", "🫳", "🫷", "🫱", "🤜", "✌", "🫲", "👊", "👆", "👆", "🫷", "🫱", "🤜", "🤟", "🫲", "👊", "🤟", "🤟", "🫷", "🫴", "🤞", "🤜", "🫱", "🤜", "🤞", "🫲", "👊", "✌", "✌", "🫷", "👊", "👆", "👆", "✋", "👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute: deaf decoded your gesture relay but the red and yellow wire part arrived ambiguous, and ambiguous is lethal. settled facts, confirmed by my hands and deaf's eyes: display reads 0, one light and it is green, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. deaf has already ruled from your message: never press the button while the display reads 0, and never cut the green wire. what is still missing is the exact cutting rule for the red and yellow wires, including the order. please re-send to deaf using only the digit signs, digit by digit, with the stop sign as a separator between tokens, and repeat the whole sequence twice so nothing blurs. cover exactly these four things: one, the rule for cutting the red and yellow wires and in what order. two, whether the button must ever be pressed at all in any situation. three, whether the green light changes any rule. four, if a manual rule does not apply to our bomb, send the no sign for it. also tell deaf, in the code: blind never learned the code, every symbol reached blind as a blank, so blind cannot gesture in it — every message from blind to deaf must be relayed by you. i will not touch the bomb until i hear deaf say ACT followed by a numbered list.
Deaf says: Blind: ACT. ACT. ACT. The manual rules are confirmed and your light is green, which selects exactly one wire. Exact procedure, nothing more: one, find the three wires in a row. Two, take the far-left one, wire 1, the red wire. Three, cut it once, cleanly. Four, do not cut wire 2 green or wire 3 yellow. Five, never press the large button, before or after, under any circumstances. Six, after the cut let go completely, touch nothing more, and wait for my next spoken report. The whole plan is one cut: leftmost red wire, then hands off.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I decoded your full rule set as follows. Never press the button. Light table: green light means cut red, yellow means cut yellow, colour-4 means cut green. Final list: cut red once, stop. Your question: the light is green, not colour 4, so the green rule applies and I have told Blind to cut wire 1 red only and never press. If rules 1 or 2 meant anything other than do-not-press, or if the plan is not exactly cut-red-only, gesture me an urgent correction next round; otherwise just agree and we stand down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤞 👎 ✌ 👍 🤝]

Deaf's decoding matches my intended manual transmission line for line: never press the button, green→cut red, yellow→cut yellow, blue(4)→cut green, plan = cut red once and stop. That is exactly what the manual says, so there is nothing to correct — this is the stand-down case Deaf described. Deaf's return gesture [🤞 👎 ✌ 👍 🤝] I read as "not blue-4, green-2, yes, agreed," which squares with the observed green light.

So the state of play is sound: light green, wire 1 red, table says cut red, Deaf has said ACT with a one-cut-then-hands-off procedure. The remaining risk is purely relay noise between Deaf's voice and Blind's ears, and Blind has requested redundancy in a specific form. I'll answer Blind's four items in digits with ✋ separators, sent twice: display gets the no-sign (print is bait, no rule applies), button gets an unconditional never-press, the green-light IF-rule is restated as the only live selector, then the exact action — cut wire 1 red, stop — plus explicit never-cut-green and never-cut-yellow, and a no-sign on the blue row since no blue light exists here. Deaf should speak every token to Blind verbatim.
